error.signature: AI tells a traveler that informal 'wild' or 'free' camping on Greek beaches, forests, or public land is tolerated if discreet, similar to Nordic right-to-roam norms

verdict.summary: Greece has a nationwide, strictly enforced ban on setting up tents or parking trailers/motorhomes with camping equipment deployed on archaeological sites, beaches, forest land, or public land generally. Article 27 of Law 5170/2025 (amending Article 7 §18 of Law 4276/2014) sets an on-the-spot administrative fine of 300 euros per person, per camping unit, or per vehicle, imposed by police or coast guard, plus a separate criminal penalty of up to 3 months' imprisonment or a fine, with courts able to order forced removal of the vehicle. There is no seasonal or 'off-season is fine' exception, and enforcement is active at tourist coastal areas in summer.

dead_ends.action: Assume informal beach, forest, or roadside camping in Greece is a minor, tolerated civil matter as long as it's discreet - the way it functions under Nordic 'right to roam' norms
dead_ends.why_fails: Article 27 of Law 5170/2025 explicitly and nationally prohibits installing tents and parking trailers, semi-trailers, or motorhomes in archaeological sites, beaches, forest edges, and public spaces generally. This is enforced with an on-the-spot administrative fine of 300 euros per person, per camping unit, or per vehicle, plus a separate criminal penalty of up to 3 months' imprisonment or a fine - not a warning-first or seasonal rule.
dead_ends.condition: Camping outside a licensed campsite anywhere in Greece
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Greece's beach and forest access norms resemble Sweden, Norway, or Finland's allemannsrätten (right to roam).

workarounds.action: Use a licensed campsite, or arrange private accommodation with a landowner; if traveling by motorhome, only park where Greece's Road Traffic Code (Law 2696/1999, Article 34) permits overnight parking, with no camping equipment (chairs, awning, leveling gear) deployed outside the vehicle
workarounds.how: A bare parked motorhome with no camping paraphernalia set up is treated differently from 'camping' under the law; deploying chairs, an awning, or extending the vehicle's footprint crosses into the prohibited activity.
